newsitem.title: USA: DuPont Merck wants tight FDA standards.
newsitem.headline: DuPont Merck wants tight FDA standards.

text.p: DuPont Merck, a joint venture between Merck Co and Dupont Co, said on Tuesday that it asked the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to tighten generic approval standards for a generic anti-coagulant drug to ensure patient safety.
Barr Laboratories is seeking FDA approval to market Warfarin Sodium tablets, a generic version of DuPont Merck's Coumadin anti-coagulant.
Barr said DuPont Merck was allegedly trying to delay Warfarin's approval to protect Coumadin and had asked the FDA to change the product's bioequivalence guidelines.

DuPont Merck said in a statement that it had asked the FDA to tighten its standards to "require that any generic warfarin product adhere to the same tight standards presently used to manufacture Coumadin."
The joint venture said it asked the FDA to tighten standards on all so-called narrow therapeutic index drugs, which require very precise dosages.
DuPont Merck said it had been in contact with the FDA for nearly a year on the matter.
